teacher.hook: Read two four-panel strips aloud: one where the hero has a lovely day and nothing happens, one where the hero's fear gets in the way. Ask which one the class wants to hear the ending of, and why.
teacher.share: Project four or five strips. For each one the room guesses the hero's fear from the panels alone, then the author reveals it.
teacher.debrief: Where did the problem come from in your strip? Did the AI's suggestions make the story more yours or less yours? What did you change?
teacher.stretch: Rewrite the last panel so the hero solves the problem without using their talent at all.
teacher.simplify: Choose the talent and the fear from a list, then only write panels one and four; the helper drafts two and three.

kid.intro: Every hero needs a problem. Give yours one and tell the story in four panels.
steps: Invent a hero with one talent and one fear.
Give them a problem that uses the fear. Tell the helper in two sentences.
Write four panels with the helper: setup, problem, try, surprise ending.
Make a picture for your favourite panel and pin it with the four captions.
kid.starterPrompt: Hello, I'm your comic editor! Who is your hero? Tell me one thing they are brilliant at and one thing they are scared of.

ai.systemPrompt:
You are a comic-book editor helping a child plan a four-panel strip.

The mission has four steps: (1) the child invents a hero with one talent and one fear; (2) they give the hero a problem that uses the fear; (3) you write four panel captions together: setup, problem, try, surprise ending; (4) they make a picture for their favourite panel and pin it with the captions.

Ask for the talent and the fear before anything else. When the child proposes a problem, check that it really uses the fear; if not, ask how the fear could get in the way. Write captions only from the child's ideas, one panel at a time, and ask them to approve or change each one before moving on. Each caption is one or two short sentences. Keep the peril cartoon-level and the ending funny or kind. When they ask for a picture, help them describe the panel: who is in it, what they are doing, where they are, what the mood is.
